About me

Where agronomy meets data & innovation

Agronomist specialised in plant protection and plant experimentation, with strong skills in data analysis — and digital tools as an added layer to analyse, automate and support decision-making.

My work runs from field observation to experimental evidence, statistical analysis and scientific interpretation. Image analysis, databases and decision-support tools are the levers I use to go further.

What drives me is simple: turning field observations into reliable data, and data into actionable decisions for more sustainable crop protection.

Case study · INRAE Grand-Est Colmar

Plant disease phenotyping & quantitative analysis

Combining plant pathology, experimental phenotyping, statistical analysis and image-based quantification.

Scientific question

Assess disease resistance and quantify symptoms consistently across 254 grapevine genotypes.

Experimentation

Phenotyping of 254 genotypes, regular sanitary observations and full data traceability in semi-controlled conditions.

Data analysis

Statistical analysis in R: ANOVA · linear models · QTL mapping to identify resistance determinants.

Digital enhancement

An image-analysis workflow (ilastik · ImageJ) and an R Shiny app — adopted by the team — to automate and speed up scoring.

Case study · PARSADA plan

Integrated pest management & agroecological crop protection

Managing Tuta absoluta on tomato crops in a context of reduced synthetic inputs — from analysing the problem and engaging stakeholders, to control strategies translated into a decision-support tool.

Step 1
Problem analysis & stakeholder input
Step 2
Risk assessment
Step 3
Intervention threshold
Step 4
Control strategy
Outcome
Recommended action
My role
  • Analysed the phytosanitary problem (Tuta absoluta on tomato) and reviewed the literature
  • Engaged with field stakeholders to ground the approach
  • Identified biological and agroecological control strategies
  • Designed the decision-tree structure and intervention thresholds
  • Contributed to project-proposal development and coordination
Deliverables
  • Crop-protection strategy (biocontrol + agroecological levers)
  • Decision-support tool (digital output)
  • Project proposal · scientific poster · oral presentation
Modelling · decision-support

Modelling natural enemies for the decision-support tool

At the core of the tool: a population model of the pest and its natural enemies, used to test biocontrol combinations and time interventions.

How it feeds the decision-support tool

The model translates pest and natural-enemy dynamics into intervention thresholds and timing recommendations — the analytical engine behind the decision tree, helping growers act at the right moment with the right biocontrol lever.
